title: Impact of comorbid mental disorders on disability pension and mortality follow-ing cardiac rehabilitation for ischemic heart disease: a routine data analysis
summary:
Cardiovascular diseases are among the leading causes of morbidity and death in Germany. Following an acute cardiac event, such as myocardial infarction, many patients participate in cardiac rehabilitation. Beyond improving physical health, cardiac rehabilitation aims to maintain work ability and facilitate patients' return to work.
Among people with heart disease, comorbid mental disorders such as depression, anxiety disorders, or severe stress reactions are common. Such psychological distress can adversely affect the further course of the disease. It may also contribute to lower levels of physical activity, less regular medication adherence, and overall greater difficulties in returning to work.
This study examines the influence of comorbid mental disorders in individuals with ischemic heart disease on disability pension and mortality.

interventions.name: We conduct our study as a retrospective cohort study. Variables describing the sample, as well as the primary and secondary outcomes, are available from administrative data. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Using the Reha-L-SUF sample, we include all mandatorily insured individuals of working age between 18 and 65 years who have a primary diagnosis of ischemic heart disease (ICD-10 I20–I25, Z95.1) and who completed cardiac rehabilitation as follow-up treatment in 2019 (rehabilitation service pursuant to Section 15 of the German Social Code Book VI).
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals who were already receiving a disability pension prior to the start of follow-up treatment are excluded.
